description:
A product's recorded daily prices over a date range. BasketWatch has kept every night's price at Aldi, Tesco, SuperValu and Dunnes Stores since May 2026 and at Lidl since 17 October 2026, and, with with_nutrition_and_ingredients, each day's nutrition per 100g or 100ml and ingredients list as the retailer's own data stated them, kept since 16 October 2026: for questions like "has the sugar in Frosties changed".

Takes product ids (as returned in product results; an Aldi id has no store prefix, and "aldi:" in front of one is accepted) or a query; with a query, the closest matching product at each shop is looked up first, one a shop, so a month of days fits whole, and each row names the product it is for. A range returns one row per product per day, and each row costs one credit; with from_date equal to to_date, one day's price is returned. One credit per row comes to about 31 for one product for a month and about 155 for a product at five shops, and a look-up by name adds one for each shop that has the product.

Every product gets the same days. When products x days would pass the row limit, the range is shortened to its most recent days for all of them and note says so; ids with no price in the range are listed in not_found.

Returns rows (id, name, store, scrape_date, price, unit_price, unit_basis, clubcard_price, offer_text, was_price), the days covered, not_found, note.

from_date.description: First day, YYYY-MM-DD. Left out: 30 days before to_date.

limit.description: Most rows to return in all (default and most 200). Fewer than products x days cuts the range to its most recent days for every product.

product_ids.description: Product ids exactly as another tool gave them, e.g. ['tesco:300793546', 'dunnes:100873410', '000000000000387044'], up to 50. The sure way to name a product.

query.description: Product name words, used when no product_ids are given: the closest match at each shop is looked up, one a shop.

store.description: One shop to look in only that one: aldi, tesco, supervalu, dunnes or lidl. Leave it out for all five.

to_date.description: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD. Left out: today.

with_nutrition_and_ingredients.description: True to add each day's nutrition per 100g or 100ml to every row, and the ingredients list on a product's first day and on any day it changed. Days before 16 October 2026 have none.

left.description: Credits left on the account after it
left.title: Left

note.description: Said when the balance is low, or when it cut this answer short
note.title: Note

used.description: Credits this answer cost: one for each record it returned
used.title: Used

clubcard_price.description: Member price that day: Tesco Clubcard, SuperValu Real Rewards or Lidl Plus
clubcard_price.title: Clubcard Price

ingredients.description: The ingredients list, on a product's first day and on any day it changed (with_nutrition_and_ingredients)
ingredients.title: Ingredients

nutrition_per_100.description: That day's nutrition per 100g or 100ml, as the retailer's own data stated it (with_nutrition_and_ingredients)

price.description: Shelf price in euro that day
price.title: Price

scrape_date.description: The day this price was recorded, YYYY-MM-DD
scrape_date.title: Scrape Date

unit_basis.description: The measure unit_price is in, as the shop states it: '1 KG', '100g', '75cl', 'each'
unit_basis.title: Unit Basis

unit_price.description: The shop's own unit price, in the measure unit_basis names: per kg at one shop, per 100g or per 75cl at another, so as it stands it does not compare across rows
unit_price.title: Unit Price

credits.description: What this answer cost the person's BasketWatch account and what is left. Missing on a free answer

not_found.description: Requested ids with no price recorded in the range: an unknown id, or a product not on sale then
not_found.title: Not Found

note.description: What was left out and why, when anything was
note.title: Note

rows.description: One row per product per day recorded, each product's days in order
